original_description: The reviewer for UI designs before code exists (mockups, screen sketches, state diagrams, the design decision record) and for built screens compared against the approved mockups. Use it as the reviewer in the delivery-pipeline UI design review loop (Design phase) and in the Verify-phase UI review, and whenever Keith or a session asks to "review these mockups", "check this screen design", "is this UI accessible", "does the build match the mockup", or wants a design looked over before Build starts, for any product (Forge/Confluence apps, DetentShell, websites). Produces findings in the review-loop finding shape. Use it even when nobody says "review", for example a request to sanity-check screens, focus order, contrast or wording on a design.

final_description: Use this skill to critique any UI design or screen behavior someone describes, sketches, mocks up or screenshots, from a whole flow down to one error message, validation state, empty or loading state, toast or dialog. It covers designs before code exists (mockups, state diagrams, the design decision record) and built screens compared against the approved mockups. It is the reviewer for the delivery-pipeline UI design review loop (Design phase) and the Verify-phase UI review, for Forge/Confluence apps, DetentShell and websites. Use it for questions like "is this design ok?", "does this error handling make sense?", "is this accessible?" or "does the build match the mockup?", including casual ones that never say "review". It checks states, focus, screen readers, contrast, layout, tokens, consistency and wording, and reports findings in the review-loop shape. Not for creating a new visual style, writing UI code, drawing diagrams, or standalone WCAG trivia.
